micah: quick check — i'm seeing a weird combo of pip/poetry issues + streaming hangs with the python sdk. project A uses poetry, my local service pip-installs the sdk editable. when streaming with the AsyncClient the connection stays open but no more tokens after 1-2 chunks, no traceback. also getting lockfile conflicts when running tox + poetry install. anyone hit this recently?
sophia: yep, lockfile conflicts are common when you mix editable pip installs with a poetry-managed repo. poetry.lock pins transitive deps (httpx, sniffio, anyio). if an editable install pulls a different httpx you'll see subtle runtime issues. try adding httpx to pyproject.toml with a compatible range then `poetry lock --no-update`. also check your HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY env vars.
james: for the streaming hang, two quick checks: 1) ensure httpx is >=0.23.0 (older httpx had stream issues). 2) make sure you don't mix sync and async clients in the same loop (eg using sync redwood.Client inside an asyncio uvicorn worker).
micah: i'm on httpx 0.23.3 and python 3.10. example usage i'm running:```python
import os
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']) as c:
        async for chunk in c.stream("generate", {"prompt": "hi"}):
            print(chunk)
```
sophia: couple more tips: set the streaming endpoint timeout to None (or a high value) and enable retries/backoff. sample config: `retries={"max_attempts": 3, "backoff_factor": 0.25}`. if you see the socket open but stalled it's often httpx + proxy or event-loop mismatch.
rachel: typing note: for consumers use `from collections.abc import AsyncIterator` and annotate the generator `-> AsyncIterator[str]`. mypy sometimes complains if you import AsyncIterator from typing on py3.10 vs py3.8 in CI.
james: another gotcha — CI and local dev python minor versions must match. poetry's lockfile is sensitive to the python constraint in pyproject. if your CI uses 3.9 but dev uses 3.10 you'll get different transitive resolution.
micah: what's the recommended dev flow if i need editable SDK + a poetry app? pip editable inside a poetry env seems brittle.
sophia: recommended: either a) develop the SDK in its own virtualenv and publish a local wheel for the app (`python -m build` + `pip install dist/*.whl`), or b) use `poetry` for both service and sdk (e.g. `poetry add ../local-redwood-sdk` so it becomes part of the lock). if you must `pip install -e`, do that inside `poetry run` (eg `poetry run pip install -e ../sdk`) to keep the same env.
dev-bot: CI alert — pipeline redwood/devex #1243: py-sdk-integration job failed on branch feature/async-fix, see logs: http://ci.internal/redwood/1243
micah: i'll try the wheel route + pin httpx to 0.23.x and run the integration tests. if it still flakes i'll open a minimal repro. thanks :pray: 
rachel: also double-check event loop policy on windows (ProactorEventLoop) — some low-level socket behavior differs and can cause partial reads in async clients.
micah: created a tiny repro gist here: http://gist.github.com/mini-repro and opened PR #3482 with test that reproduces the hang. pinging @sophia for review.
sophia: saw the PR, will review today. :thumbsup:
micah: thanks all — i'll follow up after CI run.
